title: Three structural properties of the stability relation: intersecting chords, unstable chords, and invariant blocks
source_title: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings

standard_prerequisites.name: Stable and unstable chords
standard_prerequisites.statement: A chord is stable if it belongs to the core, equivalently if its endpoints are not removed during the reduction process; otherwise it is unstable.
standard_prerequisites.use: The three parts are statements about stability and are proved by tracking which chords can be removed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Invariant set and restricted matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set S is m-invariant if every chord of m meets S in either two or zero vertices, and res_S(m) is the restriction of m to S.
standard_prerequisites.use: The third part assumes [i,j] is m-invariant and restricts the matching to it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Short chords and reduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: The reduction process repeatedly removes short chords, i.e. chords of the form (i,i+1), together with their endpoints.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both the first and second parts argue about which chords can become short.

core_obligations: Part (1): for crossing chords (i_1,i_3) and (i_2,i_4) with i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4, show by mutual dependence that neither can be removed while the other remains, so both are stable (source line 885).

Part (2): if (i,j) is unstable then some removal makes it short, which forces every vertex between i and j to be unstable; conversely if all intermediate vertices are unstable they are eventually removed and (i,j) becomes short (source lines 886-887).
Part (3): using invariance of [i,j] and perfectness of the restriction, exhibit for every vertex i_1 in [i,j] a partner i_2 in [i,j] forming a chord (source line 889).

Restrict the matching to the stable vertices inside [i,j] and observe that the result is short-chord-free, non-crossing and perfect, hence the empty matching, so every vertex of [i,j] is unstable (source line 890).

proof_roadmap.step: Part (1) by the mutual obstruction of crossing chords.
Part (2) by the two implications between instability of a chord and instability of its inner vertices.
Part (3) by invariance, the empty-matching classification and the resulting instability.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:properties of core` at source lines 873-881: intersecting chords are stable, a chord is stable if and only if some intermediate vertex is stable, and a perfect non-crossing restriction to an invariant block consists entirely of unstable chords. The author's proof (source lines 883-893) treats the three parts separately and the third is not a formality: after using the definition of invariance to pair each vertex of the block with another vertex of the block (line 889), it restricts the matching to the stable vertices of the block and observes that this restricted matching is short-chord-free, non-crossing and perfect, so it must be the empty matching (line 890). The first two parts are argued by tracking what can be removed: crossing chords cannot be removed one without the other (line 885), and instability of a chord is equivalent to all inner vertices being unstable (lines 886-887).
